newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian shares pulled up by Unibanka.
newsitem.headline: Latvian shares pulled up by Unibanka.

text.p: Latvian shares were pulled up by Unibanka by the close on Tuesday after the successful auction of one million of the state's shares in the bank, dealers said.
Total turnover came to 133,000 lats against 72,000 lats and the Riga bourse index added 4.39 points to 383.06. The Rietumu Bank index rose by 0.91 percent to 150.49.
"The market is going through stable, slowish summer trade," said Aldis Sipols, head of securities at Savings Bank.
His outlook was positive but he said the new government of Guntar Krasts, chosen yesterday to replace outgoing Prime Minister Andris Shkele, needed to keep up with privatisation.

"Provided the new government keeps the current privatisation programme intact, further Western investment may be expected in the autumn, with Ventpils Nafta (oil terminal) hopefully up for grabs," he said.
Unibanka edged up to 3.27 lats from 3.21 lats after one million of its shares were sold for 3.22 lats on Monday.
Among other shares, pharmaceutical producer Olainfarm closed at 2.45 lats, a rise from 2.38 lats, while confectionary maker Staburadze was the only official list loser, down one santime to 2.74 lats.
Olainfarm led the market, registering turnover of 73,100 lats and Unibanka had volume of 15,500 lats.
